# HOLDING CELL ACCOUNTS (ONE THREAD, ALL COLONIES) [color=#7A6F68]Pinned. One account per post. Date, time in, time out, what was done, what was written down afterwards.[/color]
### #1 pumphouse_7 (OP) // 83.03.14 Picked up after a shoving match outside the canteen. Not proud of it. I had been drinking and so had he. Two colony security officers took me, nobody took him.
Cuffed behind. Put in the small room at the end of the holding corridor, not the drunk tank. The camera in the corner had its little light off. One officer held my shoulders while the other used the baton, low on the back, both sides. Kidneys. He knew where to hit so it would not show above a belt. Nobody asked me a question the whole time. That is the part I keep coming back to. There was nothing they wanted to know.
Out at shift change, 0600. No charge. My property bag came back without my ration card. The form I signed said [italic]detained for intoxication, released without incident.[/italic]
I pissed blood for two days.
### #2 nurse_on_nights // 83.03.14 I work the clinic overnight. I will not say which one.
We see this. Not every week, but often enough that we have a word for it among ourselves. Bruising across the lower back and flanks, sometimes the backs of the thighs, nothing on the face. They always come in after release, never before, and they always say they fell. If you came in, I hope the person on shift wrote [italic]consistent with blunt trauma[/italic] and not [italic]consistent with a fall.[/italic] We are told to write what the patient says. Some of us write what we see. Ask to read your chart before you leave.
Also: blood in the urine for more than two days is not something to sleep off. Come back in.
### #3 brick_and_mortar // 83.03.15 Not to be that guy, but you said yourself you were drunk and shoving. What did you think happens? They are three officers for two thousand people. They do not have time to be gentle.
### #4 pumphouse_7 (OP) // 83.03.15 I am not saying I was polite. I am saying I was cuffed. Once your hands are behind your back the fight is over. Everything after that is something else.
### #5 ex_csec_44 // 83.03.16 Did four years in colony security on two worlds. Most of the people I worked beside would never do this, and would not have stopped it either, which is its own problem.
Some things that might help people reading: - The light on the camera going dark does not mean the camera is broken. It means someone switched the recorder to standby. There is a log of when standby is switched on. Ask for it by date in your complaint. They will say it does not exist. It does. - The small room is used because it is the only cell with no shared wall. You will not have a witness in there. - The officers who do this end up on the night roster, because nobody else wants nights. So it clusters. If you are picked up after midnight, it is a different office from the one that works days. - Officers are rated on detentions and on quiet. Nobody is rated on how people walk out.
I am not telling you this to excuse it. I am telling you so your complaint asks the right questions.
### #6 drunk_tank_regular // 83.03.18 Been in the big tank more times than I can count. It is a bench and a drain and a bucket and you get yelled at, that is all. Never been in the small room. Now I know why the guys who come out of the small room never tell anyone about the small room.
### #7 ledger_keeper (mod) // 83.03.18 Removed a post that gave an officer's first name and the hab he lives in. I know why you wrote it. I would have written it too. Rule one is not there to protect him. It is there so that when this record is read, nobody can say it was a hit list.
Badge numbers and shift times only. They are enough. Badge numbers do not move house.
### #8 quiet_daughter // 83.03.29 Different colony, different badge. A CMB deputy picked up my father because the Company liaison wanted to ask him about a missing crate from the depot he runs. They held him three days. No charge, no lawyer, no clinic. The deputy said it was protective custody. Protective of what?
He came home with a cut over his eye that he says was the cot. He is sixty one and he does not lie well. The crate turned up in the liaison's own office a week later.
### #9 ex_csec_44 // 83.03.29 Protective custody has a time limit and it has to be logged with the Marshal by the end of the shift. Three days with no log entry is not a grey area. If you can get the log, it is the thing that hangs them, not the cut.
### #10 observer_k // 83.05.02 I was posted out here as an Investigation Rights Observer. Some of you have met me. I am allowed in holding during daylight hours with notice, which tells you most of what you need to know.
I have written up nine accounts from this thread that match clinic dates. They went up to the Bureau on two separate ships. Both came back marked [italic]noted.[/italic] I do not know who reads them. I am going to keep sending them, and I am going to keep the receipts, and I would like the people in this thread to keep theirs.
To pumphouse_7: your ration card was found in a drawer in the small room, with six others. I have a list of the names on them. I will not post it.
